guidelineReference: SJA First Aid / fractures and hypothermia
title: Lower leg fracture at a protest
setting: City centre protest on a cold December day. Female caught her leg between train and platform earlier, now in severe pain, cold, showing signs of hypothermia.
verdictExplanation: Lower leg fracture with severe pain, hypothermia (34.4°C), and hypotension (85/57). Sick: call 999 immediately, immobilize, and actively warm.

shared.circulation: Skin is pale, cold, and shivering

history.history: Caught and twisted leg between train and platform earlier, walked awkwardly to protest, collapsed in pain
history.injuries: Fractured lower leg, swelling and tenderness, non-weight bearing
history.additional: Sitting outside in the cold for 20 minutes, shivering

followUp.question: What is the priority first aid intervention for this patient?

options.text: Call 999 immediately, cover her with warm blankets to treat hypothermia, and immobilize the leg
Encourage her to complete the march to keep her warm
Apply a cold ice pack to her leg and do not cover her
Force her to stand and walk to the nearest first aid tent

followUp.explanation: Suspected lower leg fracture with moderate hypothermia (34.4°C). Call 999 immediately. Cover her with warm blankets and shield from the wind to treat hypothermia. Immobilize the leg. Never apply ice to a hypothermic patient or make them walk.

levelFlags.cfaNotes: Call 999. Keep her warm with blankets. Support the leg and avoid movement.
levelFlags.erNotes: Suspected lower leg fracture and moderate hypothermia. Monitor airway. Apply splint. Warm actively with blankets/space blankets. Administer oxygen if SpO₂ <94%. Transport priority.
